selected_primary_idea.title: Sleep Function Causal Atlas
selected_primary_idea.abstract: A repeated-measures, multimodal and factorial framework that separates homeostatic pressure, circadian phase, sleep continuity, stage microstructure, and individual physiology, then maps them to domain-specific cognitive, immune, clearance, and systemic outcomes.
selected_primary_idea.research_object: Sleep as a decomposed, time-dependent physiological state and its causal effects on declared memory, immune, and maintenance phenotypes
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: Sleep pressure, circadian timing, stage microstructure, continuity, and body state jointly shape neural plasticity, memory consolidation, immune regulation, and cellular maintenance, with partially dissociable effects.
selected_primary_idea.intervention: Safe, approved perturbations of sleep opportunity and timing, with stage-resolved observation and endpoint-specific recovery schedules; no intervention executed in this artifact.
falsification_conditions: no separable timing or prior-wake effects
effects vanish under arousal and practice controls

high_risk_ideas.title: Cross-domain sleep utility state
high_risk_ideas.value: Tests whether one intervention can jointly recover memory and immune endpoints without hidden tradeoffs

rejected_ideas.title: Memory-only sleep theory
rejected_ideas.reason: Cannot explain immune, systemic, and maintenance evidence and treats heterogeneous memory as one endpoint

rejected_ideas.title: Clearance-only sleep theory
rejected_ideas.reason: Candidate clearance mechanisms do not establish a universal purpose or explain all cognitive and systemic effects

rejected_ideas.title: Duration-only predictor
rejected_ideas.reason: Discards circadian timing, stage composition, continuity, prior wake, and individual state

mcts_trace.defect: sleep need is treated as one scalar
mcts_trace.edit: separate duration, continuity, timing, stages, and wake history

mcts_trace.defect: memory benefit is treated as all-purpose explanation
mcts_trace.edit: add immune, clearance, metabolic, and cardiovascular endpoints
use factorial repeated-measures perturbation and recovery

mcts_trace.defect: population average hides responders and tradeoffs
mcts_trace.edit: add hierarchical individual-response model and safety gates
